result:
I've built the workbook and saved it as `extraction/stec.xlsx`, with the four sheets in the required order: Deal ledger (66 rows), Rounds (2), Questions (7) and Deal facts. A script confirmed that every quotation appears word for word in the filing, that each bid row has all its required columns filled, that question flags match the rows each question lists, and that Sort dates never go backwards.

**How the sale went.** sTec's board started a review of strategic alternatives, including a sale, in mid-November 2012, with an activist shareholder (Balch Hill) pressing it from December. It set up a special committee on 02/13/2013. Companies A, B, C and D approached before any adviser was hired. On 03/26/2013 the board hired BofA Merrill Lynch and decided to approach strategic buyers confidentially, which is where round 1 opens; BofA began contacting buyers on 04/01. It talked to 18 prospective acquirers:
- **Confidentiality agreements:** six parties signed one: Companies D, E, F, G and H, plus WDC through an addendum to an existing agreement.
- **Dropped out early:** Companies E and F said they only wanted certain assets, and Company G withdrew on the 05/03 due date for first-round offers.
- **First-round offers:**
  - WDC: $6.60–$7.10.
  - Company D: first said orally it would pay more than $5.60, then $5.75 in writing, a week late.
  - Company H: $5.00–$5.75.
- **Final round (from 05/16):**
  - WDC bid $9.15 with its own edits to the draft merger agreement, and the board chose it on 05/30.
  - WDC pulled back "at that time" on 05/31. Company D missed both final-round due dates and dropped out on 06/05.
  - WDC came back on 06/10 at $6.60–$7.10. The board refused to consider a range, and WDC offered $6.85 as its best and final price on 06/14.
- **Outcome:** signed 06/23/2013, announced 06/24/2013.

**Questions, with my recommendations:**
- **Q1, process and round map:** I recommend one process. The only long silence (Company A on 11/14/2012 to Company B on 02/13/2013) fails the "real break" test. Round 1 opens 03/26/2013 and round 2 on 05/16/2013. The 05/29 best-and-final request and the 06/11 demand for a single price stay inside round 2.
- **Q2, who counts as a whole-company bidder:** Company C wanted only assets from the start, so it stays outside the count. Companies E and F entered by signing agreements for a sale of the whole company, then withdrew when they switched to wanting only assets.
- **Q3, the 05/03 due date:** Extended (late bid accepted), because Company D's late offer was taken and it was allowed to continue.
- **Q4, the round-2 due dates:** 05/28 was Extended; 05/30 was Enforced.
- **Q5, Company H:** no exit when it was told its range was too low, because it was invited to revise. I recorded an inferred "not selected at signing", with the reason "would not improve earlier offer".
- **Q6, WDC's bids:** all three are Formal, and their conditions are Unclear. A reading of WDC's demand for the founders' side agreements as a make-or-break condition would make the 05/28 bid Heavy instead.
- **Q7, WDC's 05/31 pull-back:** recorded as a withdrawal, with a re-entry on 06/10.

**What I could not settle:**
- **Who is in the group of 18:** the filing doesn't say whether Companies C, E, F and G are among the 18 parties BofA talked to. The group of 14 contacted technology companies is an exact subtraction (18 minus the financial sponsor and Companies A, D and H), but I couldn't place those four in it.
- **Missing dates:** the filing gives no date for when WDC's original confidentiality agreement was signed, and no firm latest date for Company E's withdrawal.
- **Financing:** no bid had a stated financing position when it was made. That the signed agreement has no financing condition is recorded only on the signing row.
- **Filing date:** the proxy is dated 08/07/2013; 08/08/2013 comes from the file name.
